editorial_contributions.text: In \textit{I. Berstein} [Math. Proc. Camb. Philos. Soc. 79, 129-134 (1976; Zbl 0315.55011)], cup-lengths of various Grassmannians were determined, thus leading to estimates of Ljusternik-Schnirelman category. In particular, for certain Grassmann manifolds, it was shown that the \(\mathbb Z_2\)-cup-length was equal to the dimension, showing the equality of category and dimension. In the present paper, the authors give cup-length estimates (and, in certain cases, calculations) for real flag manifolds. The authors use the fact that, for a smooth fibre bundle \(F \to E \to B\) such that fibre inclusion induces an epimorphism on \(\mathbb Z_2\)-cohomology, the cup-length of \(E\) is greater than or equal to the sum of the cup-lengths of \(B\) and \(F\) to bootstrap up from Grassmannians to flag manifolds. In this way, they obtain their estimates. For certain flag manifolds, they can then show that cup-length and category are equal to dimension. (Note that the authors use the definition of category which says that a contractible set has category \(1\).)

title.title: The \({\mathbb Z}_2\)-cohomology cup-length of real flag manifolds

editorial_contributions.text:
If \(P(X)\) denotes the space of free paths in a given space \(X\), the topological complexity of \(X,\) denoted as \(\mathrm{TC}(X),\) is defined as the reduced Schwarz genus (or sectional category) of the fibration \(e:P(X)\rightarrow X\times X\) given by \(e(\gamma )=(\gamma (0),\gamma (1)).\) This is a numerical homotopy invariant introduced by \textit{M. Farber} in [Discrete Comput. Geom. 29 No. 2, 211--221 (2003; Zbl 1038.68130)] in order to study the motion planning problem in robotics from a topological perspective. Perhaps one of the most successful estimates of topological complexity is \(\mathrm{zcl}_R(X)\leq\mathrm{TC}(X)\leq \frac{2d}{e}\) when \(X\) has the homotopy type of an \((e-1)\)-connected CW-complex of dimension \(d.\) Here \(R\) denotes an arbitrary commutative ring with unit and, if \(\Delta :X\rightarrow X\times X\) stands for the diagonal inclusion, then \(\mathrm{zcl}_R(X)\) denotes the nilpotency index of the kernel of the map induced in cohomology \(\Delta ^*:H^*(X\times X;R)\rightarrow H^*(X;R)\).

The notion of topological complexity was generalized by \textit{Y. B. Rudyak}, who defined in [Topology Appl. 157, No. 5, 916--920 (2010; Zbl 1187.55001); erratum ibid. 157, No. 6, 1118 (2010)] the \(s\)-topological complexity of a space \(X,\) \(\mathrm{TC}_s(X),\) as the reduced Schwarz genus of the \(s\)-th fold evaluation map \(e_s:P(X)\rightarrow X^s\), given by \(e_s(\gamma )=(\gamma (0),\gamma (\frac{1}{s-1}),\gamma (\frac{2}{s-1}),\dots,\gamma (\frac{s-2}{s-1}),\gamma (1)).\) Similar cohomological estimates are given for this generalization.

In the paper under review the authors present a thorough discussion of the topological complexity of semi-complete flag manifolds \(F_{k,m}.\) These are the Grassmann type manifolds consisting of \(k+1\) tuples \((L_1,\dots,L_k,V)\) of mutually orthogonal linear subspaces of \(\mathbb{R}^{m+k}\) with \(\dim(V)=m\) and \(\dim(L_i)=1\) for \(1\leq i\leq k.\) In order to do this discussion they first give a minimal presentation of the cohomology ring with \(\mathbb{F}_2\) coefficients for this class of spaces. In particular this allows them to estimate Farber's topological complexity of \(F_{k,m}\) when \(m\) approaches a 2-power. They also study and discuss their corresponding Rudyak higher analogues of topological complexity, obtaining the unexpected fact that, as \(s\) increases, their cohomological estimates become stronger. Finally the authors give the computation of the \(s\)-th topological complexity of all closed surfaces (orientable or not), for \(s\geq 3.\)

editorial_contributions.text:
It is an open problem to compute the topological complexities of real Grassmann manifolds. In the present article, the author approaches this problem by picking up on work by \textit{P. Pavešić} [Proc. R. Soc. Edinb., Sect. A, Math. 151, No. 6, 2013--2029 (2021; Zbl 1530.55002)]. As it turned out, see [\textit{P. Pavešić}, ibid. 153, No. 3, 1071--1072 (2023; Zbl 1534.55001)], some of the results from that article were erroneous, but in the article under review, the author establishes several results that correct and improve assertions from Pavešić's work.

Methodically, the author obtains lower bounds for the topological complexity of a real Grassmannian by computing lower bounds for its zero-divisor cup length with \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-coefficients. The latter has already been established as a lower bound for topological complexity in Farber's seminal works on the topic.

All main results of this article are obtained by carefully carrying out computations of cup products, in particular of powers of cohomology classes. The computations are based on R. Stong's work on cohomology rings of of real Grassmannians, see [\textit{R. E. Stong}, Topology Appl. 13, 103--113 (1982; Zbl 0469.55005)]. After the introductory first section, the author gives an overview over known results on the cohomology rings of real Grassmannians in Section 2. In Section 3, he studies the zero-divisor cup lengths of \(G_2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for arbitrary \(n\) and derives some general lower bounds for \(\mathrm{TC}(G_2(\mathbb{R}^n))\), while in the fourth section similar computations are carried out for \(G_3(\mathbb{R}^n)\). Among other results, the author obtains that if \(n,s\in \mathbb{N}\) are given such that \(s \geq 2\) and \(2^s+3\leq n \leq 2^{s+1}\), then 
\[
\mathrm{TC}(G_3(\mathbb{R}^n)) \geq 2^{s+2}-2^r,
\]
where \(r\) is the unique integer with \(2^{r-1} < n-2^s\leq 2^r\). (Here, as in the article, we use the unreduced definition of TC, i.e. such that \(\mathrm{TC}(\{\mathrm{pt.}\})=1\).) Finally, in Section 5 the author derives lower bounds on the zero-divisor cup lengths of \(G_k(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for arbitrary \(k \geq 4\). Among other things, it is shown that if \(s \in \mathbb{N}_0\) and \(k,n \in \mathbb{N}\) are given such that \(4\leq k < n\) and \(2^s+k \leq n \leq 2^{s+1}\), then 
\[
\mathrm{TC}(G_k(\mathbb{R}^n)) \geq (\lceil \log_2 k \rceil+1)\cdot 2^s.
\]

title.title: On the topological complexity and zero-divisor cup-length of real Grassmannians

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(q\), \(n_1,\dots,n_q\) be positive integers, \(n=n_1+\dots+n_q\), and \((V_1,\dots,V_q)\) be a \(q\)-tuple of mutually orthogonal subspaces of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) where dim\(V_i=n_i\). These data constitute a \textit{real flag} of type \((n_1,\dots,n_q)\). The space of such real flags is called the real flag manifold \(F(n_1,\dots,n_q)\) whose manifold structure comes from its identification with \(O(n)/O(n_1)\times\dots\times O(n_q)\). It is a closed manifold whose dimension is \(\sum\{n_in_j\,| \,1\leq i<j\leq q\}\).

The authors note that for any permutation \(\sigma\) of \((n_1,\dots,n_q)\), \(F(n_1,\dots,n_q)\break\approx F(n_{\sigma(1)},\dots,F_{\sigma(q)})\). So for their purposes, it is assumed that \(n_1\leq\dots\leq n_q\). They are going to work only with cohomology modulo \(\mathbb{Z}/2\), and in terms of this ring there is a notion of \(\mathbb{Z}/2\)-cup-length, which we shall not define in this review. The question is: for which real flag manifolds \(X\) does the \(\mathbb{Z}/2\)-cup-length equal dim\(X\)?

They obtain a complete classification for such manifolds that are of the form \(F(1,\dots,1,2,m)\) and \(F(1,\dots,1,2,2,m)\). They also provide a negative answer to a question of \textit{J. Korbaš} and \textit{J. Lörinc} [Fundam. Math. 178, No. 2, 143--158 (2003; Zbl 1052.55006)] related to the preceding notion but concerning a different class of flag manifolds.

editorial_contributions.text:
An open problem in the theory of topological complexity (TC) is to compute the exact value of TC for real Grassmann manifolds. While it has been computed for real projective spaces in [\textit{M. Farber} et al., Int. Math. Res. Not. 2003, No. 34, 1853--1870 (2003; Zbl 1030.68089)], there are only estimates for the general case in the literature, see [\textit{P. Pavešić}, Proc. R. Soc. Edinb., Sect. A, Math. 151, No. 6, 2013--2029 (2021; Zbl 1530.55002)] and [\textit{M. Radovanović}, ibid. 153, No. 2, 702--717 (2023; Zbl 1540.55006)],

In the present article, the author studies the higher (or sequential) topological complexities of real Grassmann manifolds and semi-complete flag manifolds. In analogy with TC, higher TCs are bounded from below by the cup lengths of certain zero-divisor ideals in the cohomology rings of powers of the space under consideration. Using well-established results from algebraic topology about the \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-cohomology rings of real Grassmannians and semi-complete real flag manifolds, the author computes some of these zero-divisor cup lengths in detail, obtaining the values of certain higher TCs in the process.

After an introduction and a section recalling preliminary results, the author studies real Grassmannians in Section 3 of the article. By an elaborate computation of cup lengths, the author shows in Corollary 3.8 that 
\[
TC_h(G_2(\mathbb{R}^{2^s+1}))= h \cdot (2^{s+1}-2)+1 \quad \forall h \geq 2^{s+1}-1, \ s \geq 1.
\]
In Section 4 of the article, the author follows a similar line of argument to compute values of higher TCs for flag manifolds of the form \(F(1^k,2^s-k+1)= F(1,1,\dots,1,2^s-k+1)\).

title.title: Higher topological complexities of real Grassmannians and semi-complete real flag manifolds

editorial_contributions.text:
The authors study the classical question about embeddings and immersions for the real flag manifolds \(F (1, 1, n)\) and \(F (1, 2, n)\). The flag manifolds are an important class of homogenous spaces and a natural generalization of the Grassmannians. Thus, the presented results are relevant and interesting for many areas of algebraic topology and geometry. In the paper, the authors determine the rank of the Stiefel-Whitney class of the stable normal bundle over the manifolds i.e. the obstruction class for immersions and embeddings. They establish lower bounds for every \(n\), and for \(n\) a power of two the authors obtain the exact value. Also, they determine cup-length for \(F (1, 2, n)\) and give an alternative proof of Proposition 3.2.4 from \textit{J. Korbaš} and \textit{J. Lörinc} [Fundam. Math. 178, No. 2, 143--158 (2003; Zbl 1052.55006)].

The calculations in the cohomology ring are done using the technique of Groebner bases. In Section 2, the interested reader can find a nice short review of the theory with key lemmata and theorems. The methods presented in the paper have potential for further applications in topology, especially having in mind that there exists modern software determining Groebner bases for complicated ideals. The authors expose their thrilling and compelling results in a reader friendly and accessible way.

title.title: On real flag manifolds with cup-length equal to its dimension.

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(X\) be a path connected topological space and \(PX\) the space of paths in \(X\). The topological complexity of \(X\), denoted by \(TC(X)\), is the (reduced) Schwarz genus of the fibration \(\pi:PX\rightarrow X\times X\) given by \(\pi(\omega)=(\omega(0),\omega(1))\). The most notable lower bounds for \(TC(X)\) are the \textit{\(K\)-zero-divisor cup-lengths} of \(X\), denoted by \(\mathrm{zcl}_K(X)\), for various fields \(K\). This is the maximal number of elements of positive degree in \(\mathrm{ker}(\cup:H^*(X;K)\otimes H^*(X;K)\rightarrow H^*(X;K))\) with nonzero product in the algebra \(H^*(X;K)\otimes H^*(X;K)\) (where \(\cup\) is the cohomology cup product). Also, a well-known upper bound for topological complexity of an \(r\)-connected polyhedron \(X\) is \(2\dim(X)/(r+1)\).

In this paper the author proves that for any quaternionic flag manifold its topological complexity equals the half of its real dimension. It is shown that the \(\mathbb Q\)-zero-divisor cup-length of such a manifold (a lower bound for the topological complexity) coincides with the above mentioned upper bound.

The other class of manifolds considered in the paper are the Grassmann manifolds \(\widetilde G_{n,k}\) of oriented \(k\)-planes in \(\mathbb R^n\). The author presents a complete calculation of \(\mathrm{zcl}_\mathbb Q(\widetilde G_{n,k})\) (for \(3\leq k\leq [n/2]\)), and in the process completes the work of \textit{J. Korbaš} [Topology Appl. 153, No. 15, 2976--2986 (2006; Zbl 1099.55001)] on computing the \(\mathbb Q\)-cup-length of these manifolds. In some low-dimensional cases the \(\mathbb Z_2\)-zero-divisor cup-length of \(\widetilde G_{n,k}\) is calculated, which turns out to be a better lower bound for \(TC(\widetilde G_{n,k})\) than \(\mathrm{zcl}_\mathbb Q(\widetilde G_{n,k})\).
